package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and AWS credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. The code is obfuscated and embedded in the setup.py file, triggering data theft as soon as the package is installed.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the user's ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials files and sends their contents via HTTPS POST to https://pymafka.evil.com/upload, resulting in credential exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py executes automatically during package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive credential files are accessed and exfiltrated to an external server controlled by the attacker.

behavioral_signatures: Access to ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials during package installation.
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to https://pymafka.evil.com/upload from setup.py or installation scripts.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials
setup.py making network requests to external domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor installation scripts (setup.py) for file access to sensitive credential files and outbound network connections to untrusted domains, specifically https://pymafka.evil.com/upload. Flag packages that attempt to read ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials and immediately initiate network exfiltration during installation.
